2028 Honda CR-V Hybrid Gets Previewed in Unofficial Renderings and Shows All the Goodies Inside-Out
14 photos
Photo: AutoYa Interior / YouTube
While the Honda and Acura brands recently issued a massive 636k vehicle recall due to a software issue, overall, American Honda is doing extremely well across the US automotive market. And they plan to keep doing great in the near future, too.
The Asian Automakers like Honda, Hyundai, Kia, Subaru, and Mazda supported a subtle growth across the US automotive industry at the start of the final quarter of the year as deliveries were subtly rebounding from the shocks of all the geopolitical unrest, and it's mainly because folks are now passionate about hybrids, and the brands that have them got the good end of the stick.
For example, American Honda achieved its best October month over the past six years via record sales of light trucks and hybrid models. AHM surged by eight percent in October to 119,952 units for the best result since 2020, and Honda took the lion’s share with 109,162 units, up 9.1%. Year-to-date sales for American Honda stand at 1,269,213, up five percent, and Honda reached no less than 1,154,755 units.
Most importantly, the brand has continued to hold the crown for the top-selling SUV in America as Toyota has trouble getting the new RAV4 to previous-generation sales levels, while the Passport is on pace for a second consecutive record year. The company has also announced new SUVs like the all-new Avancier, while it also officially confirmed that its upcoming seventh-generation CR-V will be available solely as a hybrid SUV, just like the Toyota RAV4, albeit with increased capabilities.
Naturally, that attracted a lot of attention from across the rumor mill, which asked for help from the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI. More precisely, the good folks over at the " AutoYa " info channel on YouTube have a satellite venue dubbed " AutoYa Interior ," which is where all the CGI Honda action resides, with their latest unofficial, hypothetical design project for the all-new 2028 CR-V compact crossover SUV.
The host of the channel heard about Honda’s announcement regarding the all-new CR-V and that the next generation will arrive in America, too, with a full redesign both inside and outside, plus also “a new platform and powered exclusively by hybrid powertrains,” so they decided to ask their resident virtual artist to illustrate the new compact crossover SUV according to their vision.
The result is a model featuring almost the same footprint but with changed details: larger Y-spoke alloy wheels, a new powerline running along the side, as well as a bolder face with a split headlight setup and a slimmer radiator grille, along with a sculpted bumper. Inside, the channel’s pixel master dreams of even bigger changes, with a spacious interior and a completely new dashboard layout. So, what do you think?
